title: Threat modeling friction and secrets triage — sync notes 2026-11-18
content:
Meeting: Security Engineering Sync — Threat modeling friction & secrets triage
Date: 2026-11-18 10:00–11:00 PT (standup + extended discussion)
Facilitator: Nora Kline
Attendees: Nora Kline, Arjun Patel, Lina Ortega, Maya Chen, Devon Price, Samir Rao + SRE repr (brief)
Context / goal: Reconcile current vuln queue (external scans + fuzzing results), review two recent secrets near-miss findings, and surface friction points in our threat-modeling process that slow down rollout of mitigations for Dedicated/Private customers. Rapid decisions and clear owners are the priority.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Triage backlog reduced by 13 items after reclassification; 5 remain P1/P1+.
- Secrets near-miss (CI artifact exposure) contained; follow-up items on CI hygiene and ephemeral credential adoption created.
- Threat-modeling bottlenecks: lack of template alignment between product & infra, and slow dependencies on applied-ml for model-specific attack surface input. Immediate mitigations accepted: triage checklist update + quarterly threat-modeling office hours.

Notes / discussion items:
1) Vulnerability triage snapshot
- New inbound items: OSS dependency alerts from SCA (4), fuzzing-derived crashers reported by research (2), internal code-scan matches flagged by SAST (3).
- Rapid decisions:
  - SCA findings (low severity transitive deps) -> deferred; add to weekly dependency-remediation sprint (owner: DevOps squad, due: 2026-12-08). (Refs: SEC-9123)
  - Fuzzing crashers (applied-ml model loader path) -> mark P1 until root cause identified. Arjun to run reproducer locally (SEC-PR-984).
  - SAST true-positive in session-deserialization -> immediate patch PR (runtime#984). Apply hotfix to prod-dedicated staging lane; SRE to validate roll-forward policy. Owner: Lina (code owner), SRE owner: Devon. Target: 2026-11-22.
- Risk scoring notes: two items escalated to P1+ because they affect tokenization/model loading and could be abused for inference denial. Score rationale attached in ticket comments.

2) Secrets / credential hygiene (incident: CI artifact exposure — near-miss)
- What happened: A temporary artifact (build log) contained a redacted KMS request ID but not the key. Automated scanning flagged possible leakage (false positive initially). Manual review found long-lived service account token cached in internal runner image used by one pipeline. Token had permissions scoped too broadly.
- Containment: rotated token, revoked session, and replaced the runner image with ephemeral credentials built via short-lived OIDC tokens.
- Immediate follow-ups:
  - Enforce ephemeral credentials on all ephemeral runners (OPS-4410). Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-11-26.
  - Add an automated pre-merge check to block runner images that contain any known key patterns or base64 blobs >1kB. Owner: CI Platform (Maya). Due: 2026-12-02.
  - Inventory: produce a list of pipelines still using long-lived tokens. Owner: Security Tooling (Arjun). Due: 2026-11-24.
- Notes-to-self: need a short FAQ for infra teams describing OIDC -> KMS flow, common migration pitfalls, and where to get help (cc: infra Slack).

3) Threat modeling friction points (focused discussion)
- Problem statement: Product teams (console, hosted-api, dedicated) create threat models ad-hoc with varying structure; infra/serving-runtime inputs are often missing (model loading, KV cache, kernel fallback). As a result, mitigations proposed miss critical operational constraints and stall review.
- Observed frictions:
  a) Templates misaligned: product templates ask high-level goals but not low-level runtime invariants (e.g., sequence length maxima, cache eviction semantics).
  b) Timing mismatch: threat-models are requested late in cycle (post-design freeze), causing rework.
  c) Expertise gap: applied-ml must provide model-specific failure modes but is under capacity.
- Proposed immediate fixes (agreed):
  1. Introduce a lightweight runtime-focused appendix to the canonical threat model template (see Confluence: Threat Model Library). Appendix fields: model runtime invariants, KV cache behavior, fallback model variants, expected QPS/latency SLOs. Owner: Nora + Runtime eng (Arjun). Due: 2026-11-30.
  2. Quarterly "Threat Office Hours" where sec-eng + applied-ml review in-progress threat models — first session scheduled 2026-12-07. Owner: Lina.
  3. Add a gating checklist item for Dedicated/Private rollouts: a signed runtime appendix must be attached to the threat-model PR before security approval. Owner: Product Security. Enforcement date: 2027-01-03.
- Longer term: consider hiring a 0.5 FTE applied-ml security liaison (proposal to P&O in next headcount cycle).

4) Decisions made during meeting
- Adopt runtime appendix template (action above).
- Ephemeral credential migration mandated for CI runners; blocklist long-lived tokens.
- P1 fuzzing crashers will be prioritized over low-priority SCA items for immediate patch work.

5) Action items (owner / due / note)
- Arjun Patel: reproduce fuzzing crashers, attach reproducer and initial blame analysis to SEC-9123. Due 2026-11-20.
- Lina Ortega: land hotfix for deserialization SAST true-positive; coordinate staging rollout and validation with SRE. Due 2026-11-22.
- Samir Rao: rotate and revoke exposed token (complete), produce pipelines inventory and remediation plan. Due 2026-11-24.
- Maya Chen: implement CI pre-merge check for artifact patterns; document bypass process for emergencies. Due 2026-12-02.
- Nora Kline + Arjun: draft runtime appendix to Threat Model Library + example filled appendix for Dedicated model serving. Due 2026-11-30.
- Lina: schedule first Threat Office Hours and send invites to applied-ml + runtime leads. Due 2026-11-23.

6) Open questions / blockers
- Applied-ML bandwidth: who will attend office hours from applied-ml? (Action: Product Security to confirm).
- CI runner fleet ownership handoff for ephemeral credentials — need formal owner in infra. (Action: Devon to escalate in next infra sync).
- Are there regulatory constraints for older Dedicated customers that prevent rolling ephemeral creds? Need list. (Action: Customer Success to provide constraints for pinned deployments).

7) Quick wins for next two weeks
- Patch the SAST issue and validate in staging (short-term risk reduction).
- Add pre-merge CI check to prevent accidental secret inclusion.
- Publish runtime appendix and run a small pilot on one Dedicated rollout.

8) Misc / ad-hoc notes
- Reference: older "secrets-mapping" doc had useful token-scoping examples; will pull snippets into the FAQ.
- Reminder to update on-call runbook with short instructions for revoking credentials (add commands, playbook steps). Owner: SRE (Devon).
- Parking lot: start drafting policy for model-card security annotations (defer to next quarter).

Meeting artifacts / attachments: reproducer logs in SEC-9123, hotfix PR link (runtime#984), CI scan logs (internal link), Threat Model Library page link.

Status: notes/draft for internal review — pass to product security + applied-ml for alignment.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the runtime appendix intentionally short (1 page) — we want adoption not more paperwork.
- Follow up with Lina daily on the hotfix until prod validation.
- After Office Hours pilot, measure time-to-closure on threat review tickets to see if friction reduced.

End of notes.
